description:
Count the weather over Switzerland at one hour: MeteoSwiss's hourly weather symbol at all ~5800 forecast points (postal code centres, weather stations, mountain points), grouped into weather categories per MeteoSwiss forecast region and altitude band. Use it for area questions: where it is sunny, how high the fog or low stratus reaches, whether it is sunny above it, where it rains or snows. For the forecast at one place, use meteoswissLocalForecast.

Regions are MeteoSwiss's seven forecast regions: jura, mittelland (Swiss Plateau), alpennordhang (northern Alps and Prealps), wallis (Valais), engadin, nordundmittelbuenden (northern and central Grisons), alpensuedseite (southern side of the Alps: Ticino and the southern valleys of Grisons). Points outside MeteoSwiss's seven regions are counted in the nearest one.

Narrow the count with region, bbox (a WGS84 box), near (air distance around a place, at most 150 km) and min_altitude_m / max_altitude_m; given together, a point must pass all of them. With until, the count covers every hour from time to until, at most 12 hours after time (up to 13 hourly steps).

Categories: sunny, clear_night, partly_sunny, cloudy, high_cloud, fog_or_stratus, rain, sleet, snow, thunder; the answer's "legend" gives the symbol codes of each. fog_or_stratus also counts an overcast or partly sunny hour under a low cloud deck (low cloud >= 80 %, medium and high cloud < 50 %): MeteoSwiss's symbol often shows such a deck as "overcast".

Reading the answer:
- Times are local Europe/Zurich time with the UTC offset. The symbol of an hour describes the 3 hours that end at that time.
- "points" counts forecast points, not area: they are dense in towns and the lowlands and sparse in the mountains. A band with few points says little. A few places have two points (a station and a regional forecast point at the same spot); both count.
- Around sunrise and sunset MeteoSwiss switches the points from day to night symbols at different hours, so one clear sky can show as both sunny and clear_night: add them for "clear sky" at those hours.
- At high altitude fog_or_stratus usually means a summit in cloud (MeteoSwiss's own fog symbol), not a fog sea: for a fog question leave the summits out with max_altitude_m.
- Per band, "pct" holds the shares in whole percent (they add up to 100) and "dominant" the most frequent category.
- jura, mittelland and alpennordhang also carry "fog_top_m" (experimental): the top of a fog sea to the nearest 100 m: the 100 m bands that are mostly fog_or_stratus, starting with the region's lowest band (below 1000 m) up, with mostly sun in the 300 m above ("sunny_above_fog_pct"). null means no fog sea with sun above: no fog layer low down, or cloud above it. Over a window (until) all point-hours are pooled into one estimate for the whole window. For a fog question, also read the bands yourself.
- With map: "grid", "grid.rows" is a coarse map, north at the top: one character per 5 km cell, the most frequent category there ("grid.key"); "grid.cols" is the number of characters in every row and "grid.row_count" the number of rows. Use it to say where (west or east, which valleys) rather than how much. To show the user a map, use meteoswissWeatherMapExperimental if it is listed: the client then displays a ready-made map, so do not draw one yourself.
- "missing" (present only when more than 0) counts the point-hours left out because the run has no weather symbol for them. They are in no share and no count: a few change nothing, many mean the answer rests on fewer points.
- The forecast is updated hourly. Further ahead it may have symbols only every few hours; a time the run does not cover is an error that names the hours it has.

Source: MeteoSwiss Open Data; the forecast regions come from the MeteoSwiss website (Source: MeteoSwiss).

bands.description: Altitude band edges in metres, ascending, e.g. [600, 800, 1000] for a fog question; default [500, 1000, 1500, 2000] gives the bands <500, 500-999, 1000-1499, 1500-1999, >=2000. [] gives one band.

bbox.description: Only points inside this WGS84 box: [west, south, east, north] in degrees, e.g. [7.0, 46.5, 8.5, 47.5].

map.description: "grid" adds a coarse map: the most frequent category in each 5 km cell, as text rows (about 3 KB more for the whole country). Default "none".

max_altitude_m.description: Only points at or below this altitude, in m above sea level

min_altitude_m.description: Only points at or above this altitude, in m above sea level

near.description: Only points within radius_km of a place, e.g. {"lat": 47.37, "lon": 8.54, "radius_km": 40} around Zurich. Air distance, not travel time.

radius_km.description: Radius in km, air distance, at most 150

region.description: Only this MeteoSwiss forecast region: jura, mittelland (Swiss Plateau), alpennordhang (northern Alps and Prealps), wallis (Valais), engadin, nordundmittelbuenden (northern and central Grisons), alpensuedseite (southern side of the Alps, Ticino). Default: all seven.

time.description: The hour to count, in local Swiss time: "2026-11-14T10:00" (minutes are ignored). A time with a UTC offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T10:00:00+01:00" from meteoswissLocalForecast, is also accepted.

until.description: Last hour of a window, included, at most 12 h after time; same format as time. Every hour from time to until is counted: "points" stay points, the shares in "pct" are then shares of point-hours (each point once per hour).

name: meteoswissWeatherSituation

grid.description: Present only with map: "grid" and at least one point: a coarse map of the categories

cols.description: Cells per row: the length of every string in "rows"

north.description: LV95 north coordinate of the north edge of the first row, m

row_count.description: Number of rows: the length of "rows"

rows.description: One string per row of cells, north to south; character i is the cell i × cell_m east of "west". Each character is the most frequent category of the points in the cell (see "key").

west.description: LV95 east coordinate of the west edge of the rows, m

legend.description: What each category in this answer means, with its MeteoSwiss symbol codes

missing.description: Point-hours left out because the run has no weather symbol for them; present only when more than 0

regions.description: MeteoSwiss forecast regions, west to east and north to south

bands.description: Altitude bands with points, lowest first

dominant.description: The most frequent category in this band

pct.description: Share of the points (over a window: of the point-hours) per category, in whole percent, largest first; they add up to 100. Categories at 0 % are left out.

dominant.description: The most frequent category over the whole region

fog_top_m.description: Experimental. Top of a fog sea in m, to the nearest 100 m: starting at the lowest 100 m band of the region, which must be mostly fog_or_stratus (and start below 1000 m), up as long as the bands stay so, with mostly sun above. null when the points show no fog sea with sun above. Over a window (until) all point-hours of the window are pooled into one count, so the value is one estimate for the whole window, not one per hour: ask for single hours to see it change. Only for jura, mittelland and alpennordhang.

fog_top_points.description: Experimental. Points (over a window: point-hours) the fog top rests on: the fog layer and the 300 m above; null without a fog top

name.description: The region's German name as MeteoSwiss writes it

sunny_above_fog_pct.description: Experimental. Share of the points in the 300 m above fog_top_m that are sunny, partly sunny or a clear night, in whole percent; null without a fog top. Over a window it is the share of the pooled point-hours of the whole window

run.description: The forecast run the counts come from, local time with offset

from.description: First counted hour in local Europe/Zurich time with offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T10:00:00+01:00"

until.description: Last counted hour of the window, same format (the run may lack the hour asked for); present only when until was given

warnings.description: Present only when something limits the answer: a cloud cover file could not be loaded (the cloud rule is then off and fog_or_stratus counts only the fog and stratus symbols), or the run has symbols for only some hours of the window.

title: Weather situation across Switzerland
